items.followUp: Define transpiration and explain two ways in which it is significant to plants.

rubric.why: Checks that the definition identifies what is lost during transpiration.
rubric.description: Defines transpiration as the loss of water vapour.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the loss of water vapour.

rubric.why: Checks that the definition identifies where this water loss occurs.
rubric.description: States that water vapour is lost from the aerial parts of a plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the aerial parts of the plant.

rubric.description: States that transpiration cools the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the cooling effect.

rubric.why: Checks the role of transpiration in water movement.
rubric.description: Explains that transpiration pull helps move water upward through the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking transpiration pull with upward water movement.

rubric.description: States that transpiration helps transport or distribute mineral salts through the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking transpiration with mineral-salt movement.

modelAnswer: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly through the stomata.
It creates a transpiration pull that helps in the upward movement of water.
It helps transport and distribute mineral salts through the plant.
